papers.title: CloserToMe: A Unified Framework for Accurate and Transferable Latency Prediction Across Heterogeneous Devices
papers.abstract:
Hardware accelerators such as GPUs, NPUs, and FPGAs are essential to meeting AI’s computational demands. With the proliferation of heterogeneous devices across cloud and edge, various model optimization techniques adapt to diverse hardware characteristics through operator transformations and structural modifications.  Accurate, efficient latency prediction enables rapid selection of optimal strategies across hardware backends.
Many existing methods treat hardware as a black-box executor, directly regressing latency without explicitly modeling the intricate interactions between neural network (NN) structures and device-specific execution behaviors. To address these challenges, we introduce a new modeling perspective that captures the interaction between neural architectures and hardware execution. To capture device-specific characteristics, we propose two complementary modeling strategies. The Device Behavior Signature Selector (DBSel) characterizes hardware execution behavior by selectively probing a small set of representative architectures, forming a compact, workload-driven profile. In parallel, we construct capability vectors that capture the hierarchical memory of each device and compute characteristics, providing a structured abstraction of its architectural capacity. To unify both behavioral and structural views, we introduce the Hardware–Operation Dialogue Module (HODM), which models fine-grained interactions between neural operators and hardware properties. Together, these components empower CloserToMe to deliver accurate and transferable latency predictions across unseen and diverse platforms.

papers.title: KernelCraft: Benchmarking for Agentic Close-to-Metal Kernel Generation on Emerging Hardware
papers.abstract: New AI accelerators with novel instruction set architectures (ISAs) often require developers to manually craft low-level kernels — a time-consuming and error-prone process that does not scale across hardware targets. This delays emerging hardware platforms from reaching the market. While prior LLM-based code generation has shown promise in mature GPU ecosystems, it remains unclear whether agentic LLM systems can quickly produce valid and efficient kernels for emerging hardware with new ISAs. We present KernelCraft: the first benchmark for evaluating an LLM agent's ability to generate and optimize low-level kernels for customized accelerators through a function-calling, feedback-driven workflow. We evaluate agent performance across three emerging accelerators on more than 20 machine-learning tasks, each with five diverse task configurations. Across four leading reasoning models, the strongest agents generate functionally correct kernels for unseen ISAs within a few refinement steps, and produce optimized kernels that match or outperform compiler baselines. These results demonstrate KernelCraft's potential to accelerate the accelerator chip development cycle. KernelCraft is available at https://kernelcraft-cam.github.io/.

papers.title: Ladder: Enabling Efficient {Low-Precision} Deep Learning Computing through Hardware-aware Tensor Transformation
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for improving deep learning model performance has led to a paradigm shift in supporting low-precision computation to harness the robustness of deep learning to errors. Despite the emergence of new low-precision data types and optimization approaches, existing hardware and software have insufficient and inefficient support for those evolving data types, making it challenging to achieve real performance gains through low-precision computing. This paper introduces Ladder, a novel compiler designed to bridge the gap between evolving custom data types and the fixed precision formats supported by current hardware. Leveraging a general type system, tType, and an extended tensor expression, Ladder transforms deep neural network (DNN) computations into optimized computing pipelines with custom data types as the first-class citizen, exposing an optimization space for efficiently handling data storage, accesses, and type conversions. Ladder employs a new set of tensor scheduling primitives and a hardware-aware optimization policy to navigate the complex transformation space, ensuring optimal performance across different memory layers and DNN operators. Our evaluation demonstrates Ladder's capability to systematically support a wide array of low-bit precision custom data types, significantly enhancing the performance of DNN computations on modern accelerators without necessitating hardware modifications. This innovation empowers model designers with the ability to explore data type optimizations and offers hardware vendors a flexible solution to expand their support for diverse precision formats.

papers.title: HALO: Hardware-Aware Quantization with Low Critical-Path-Delay Weights for LLM Acceleration
papers.abstract: Quantization is critical for efficiently deploying large language models (LLMs). Yet conventional methods remain hardware-agnostic, limited to bit-width constraints, and do not account for intrinsic circuit characteristics such as the timing behaviors and energy profiles of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units. This disconnect from circuit-level behavior limits the ability to exploit available timing margins and energy-saving opportunities, reducing the overall efficiency of deployment on modern accelerators. To address these limitations, we propose HALO, a versatile framework for Hardware-Aware Post-Training Quantization (PTQ). Unlike traditional methods, HALO explicitly incorporates detailed hardware characteristics, including critical-path timing and power consumption, into its quantization approach. HALO strategically selects weights with low critical-path-delays enabling higher operational frequencies and dynamic frequency scaling without disrupting the architecture's dataflow. Remarkably, HALO achieves these improvements with only a few dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) adjustments, ensuring simplicity and practicality in deployment. Additionally, by reducing switching activity within the MAC units, HALO effectively lowers energy consumption. Evaluations on accelerators such as Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) demonstrate that HALO significantly enhances inference efficiency, achieving average performance improvements of 270% and energy savings of 51% over baseline quantization methods, all with minimal impact on accuracy.

papers.title: Deep Kernel Fusion for Transformers
papers.abstract: Agentic LLM inference with long contexts is increasingly limited by memory bandwidth rather than compute. In this setting, SwiGLU MLP blocks, whose large weights exceed cache capacity, become a major yet under-optimized bottleneck in the Transformer architecture. We propose DeepFusionKernel, a deeply fused kernel that cuts HBM traffic and boosts cache reuse, delivering up to 13.2% speedup on H100 and 9.7% on A100 over SGLang. Integrated with SGLang and paired with a kernel scheduler, DeepFusionKernel ensures consistent accelerations across generation lengths, while remaining adaptable to diverse models, inference configurations, and hardware platforms.

papers.title: MACKO: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication for low sparsity
papers.abstract:
Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) is a fundamental operation in the inference of sparse Large Language Models (LLMs).
Because existing SpMV methods perform poorly under the low, unstructured sparsity ($30-90\\%$) commonly observed in pruned LLMs, unstructured pruning provides only limited memory reduction and speedup.
We propose **MACKO-SpMV**, a GPU-optimized format and kernel co-designed to reduce storage overhead while remaining compatible with the GPU’s execution model.
This enables efficient SpMV for unstructured sparsity without specialized hardware units or precomputation.
We identify memory bandwidth as the primary limiting factor of SpMV and analyze the storage overhead of MACKO.
At $50\\%$ sparsity, MACKO is the first approach to achieve $1.5\times$ memory reduction and $1.2-1.5\times$ speedup over the dense baseline as well as substantial improvements over other SpMV methods: cuSPARSE ($2.8-13.0\times$), Sputnik ($1.9-2.6\times$), and DASP ($2.2-2.5\times$).
An LLM pruned with Wanda to sparsity $50\\%$ requires $1.5\times$ less memory and achieves $1.5\times$ faster inference at fp16 precision.
As a result, **unstructured pruning at $50\\%$ sparsity becomes practical** for real-world LLM workloads and **bridges the efficiency gap with structured 2:4 sparsity**.

papers.title: {MPK}: A Compiler and Runtime for {Mega-Kernelizing} Tensor Programs
papers.abstract: We introduce Mirage Persistent Kernel (MPK), the first compiler and runtime system that automatically transforms multi-GPU model inference into a single high-performance mega-kernel. MPK introduces an SM-level graph representation that captures data dependencies at the granularity of individual streaming multiprocessors (SMs), enabling cross-operator software pipelining, fine-grained overlap of computation and communication, and other optimizations that are infeasible under the conventional kernel-per-operator execution model. The MPK compiler lowers tensor programs into optimized SM-level task graphs and generates fast CUDA implementations for each task, while the MPK in-kernel parallel runtime executes these tasks within a single persistent mega-kernel using decentralized scheduling across SMs. Together, these components provide end-to-end kernel fusion with minimal developer effort, while preserving the flexibility of existing programming models. Our evaluation shows that MPK significantly outperforms existing kernel-per-operator LLM serving systems, achieving up to 1.7× lower end-to-end inference latency and pushing LLM inference performance close to the limits of the underlying hardware. MPK is publicly available at https://github.com/mirage-project/mirage .

papers.title: Parallel Scan on Ascend AI Accelerators
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) depend on model- and architecture-specific optimizations to be efficiently
executed at a large scale. The number of new LLM variants grows rapidly, making it necessary to distill and
only optimize a few common parallel computational primitives, including prefix sum (scan). In this work, we
design high-performance prefix-sum algorithms for the Ascend NPU architecture and explore their applicability
in AI workloads and LLMs. The key feature of our algorithms is the efficient use of vector and matrix units in
the Ascend architecture, which allows us to reach up to 74.9% of the memory bandwidth achieved by memory
copy. To showcase the effectiveness of matrix-multiplication-based scans as a fast primitive in AI workloads, we
implemented several essential scan-based operators like radix sort and top-p, achieving respectively up to 3.3×
and 2.3× speedup compared to the vector-only kernels. Finally, we show how these optimized kernels can impact
real world models on the Ascend NPU obtaining 2.02× speed-up on state-space neural networks like Mamba, and
up to 1.47× on LLMs with large vocabulary sizes thanks to more efficient top-p token sampling.

papers.title: FlashSinkhorn: IO-Aware Entropic Optimal Transport on GPU
papers.abstract: Entropic optimal transport (EOT) via Sinkhorn iterations is widely used in modern machine learning, yet GPU solvers remain inefficient at scale. Tensorized implementations suffer quadratic HBM traffic from dense $n\times m$ interactions, while existing online backends avoid storing dense matrices but still rely on generic tiled map-reduce reduction kernels with limited fusion. We present **FlashSinkhorn**, an IO-aware EOT solver for squared Euclidean cost that rewrites stabilized log-domain Sinkhorn updates as row-wise LogSumExp reductions of biased dot-product scores, the same normalization as transformer attention. This enables FlashAttention-style fusion and tiling: fused Triton kernels stream tiles through on-chip SRAM and update dual potentials in a single pass, substantially reducing HBM IO per iteration while retaining linear-memory operations. We further provide streaming kernels for transport application, enabling scalable first- and second-order optimization. On A100 GPUs, FlashSinkhorn achieves up to $32\times$ forward-pass and $161\times$ end-to-end speedups over state-of-the-art online baselines on point-cloud OT, improves scalability on OT-based downstream tasks. For reproducibility, we release an open-source implementation at https://github.com/ot-triton-lab/flash-sinkhorn.

papers.title: Segmented Operations using Matrix Multiplications
papers.abstract: Specialized computational units that perform small matrix multiplications as primitive operations are typically present in modern AI accelerators. However, these Matrix Multiplication Units (MMUs) are often underutilized for many fundamental deep learning operations besides dense matrix multiplications. Coincidentally, the lack of a rigorous theoretical model of computation for such architectures obstructs algorithmic design. In this work, we propose MMV-RAM, a computational model which judiciously extends the Vector-RAM model with an additional MMU. We provide a detailed theoretical analysis and carefully balance the computational power between the matrix and vector units, guided by the circuit complexity lower bound that parity is not in AC[0]. In MMV-RAM, we proceed to algorithm design, starting with two fundamental parallel operations: *segmented scan* and *sum*. By expressing them as compositions of elementary parallel primitives (e.g., seg. sum reduces to: scan, compress, and vector differentiation), we can  exploit MMUs to perform *speculative* blocked computations, ultimately leading to *provable theoretical speed-ups* against vector-only approaches. These results extend to other ubiquitous AI kernels, including dense matrix product, and sparse matrix-vector product. As a case study, we implemented the proposed algorithms on the Ascend 910B AI accelerator, which contains matrix and vector cores. We evaluate these implementations on synthetic and real-world datasets from various applications, including Large Language Models.

papers.title: QFlash: Bridging Quantization and Memory Efficiency in Vision Transformer Attention
papers.abstract:
FlashAttention improves efficiency through tiling, but its online softmax still relies on floating-point arithmetic for numerical stability, making full quantization difficult.
We identify three main obstacles to integer-only FlashAttention: (1) scale explosion during tile-wise accumulation, (2) inefficient shift-based exponential operations on GPUs, and (3) quantization granularity constraints requiring uniform scales for integer comparison.
To address these challenges, we propose QFlash, an end-to-end integer FlashAttention design that performs softmax entirely in the integer domain and runs as a single Triton kernel.
On seven attention workloads from ViT, DeiT, and Swin models, QFlash achieves up to 6.73x speedup over I-ViT and up to 8.69x speedup on Swin, while reducing energy consumption by 18.8% compared to FP16 FlashAttention, without sacrificing Top-1 accuracy on ViT/DeiT and remaining competitive on Swin under per-tensor quantization.
Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/EfficientCompLab/qflash.

papers.title: A New PPML Paradigm for Quantized Models
papers.abstract: Model quantization has become a common practice in machine learning (ML) to improve efficiency and reduce computational/communicational overhead. However, adopting quantization in privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) remains challenging due to the complex internal structure of quantized operators, which leads to inefficient protocols under the existing PPML frameworks. In this work, we propose a new PPML paradigm that is tailor-made for and can benefit from quantized models. Our main observation is that look-up tables can ignore the complex internal constructs of any functions which can be used to simplify the quantized operator evaluation. We view the model inference process as a sequence of quantized operators, and each operator is implemented by a look-up table. We then develop an efficient private look-up table evaluation protocol, and its online communication cost is only $log n$, where $n$ is the size of the look-up table. On a single CPU core, our protocol can evaluate $2^{26}$ tables with 8-bit input and 8-bit output per second. The resulting PPML framework for quantized models offers extremely fast online performance. The experimental results demonstrate that our quantization strategy achieves substantial speedups over SOTA PPML solutions, improving the online performance by $40sim 60 times$ w.r.t. convolutional neural network (CNN) models, such as AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet18, and by $10sim 25 times$ w.r.t. large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-2, GPT-Neo, and Llama2. papers.title: UQ-ViT: Harmonizing Extreme Activations with Hardware-Friendly Uniform Quantization in Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Post-Training Quantization enables efficient Vision Transformer (ViTs) deployment with a small calibration data, and its prevalent use of uniform quantization harnesses AI accelerator matrix cores for high-speed inference. However, the application of uniform quantization is fundamentally challenged by the extreme non-uniformity of activation distributions.Specifically, the power-law nature of post-Softmax attention scores and the significant inter-channel variance in post-GELU activations create a dilemma for conventional quantization, as it struggles to preserve critical high-magnitude values without sacrificing overall precision. To resolve this core conflict, we introduce UQ-ViT (Uniform Quantization for Vision Transformers), a novel uniform quantization framework designed to reconcile high precision with hardware efficiency. Central to UQ-ViT are two operators: Dynamic Elimination of Maximum (DeMax) and Normalization Quantization (NormQuant). DeMax is a quantization operator for post-Softmax attention scores that utilizes uniform quantization. It dynamically eliminates and preserves dominant values, effectively mitigating quantization loss from the extreme values in the power-law distribution. NormQuant utilizes a per-channel quantization strategy during quantization and reverts to a per-tensor format for dequantization, achieving both high accuracy and computational efficiency. Crucially, it is applicable to any linear layer, enabling effective quantization of post-GELU activations in ViTs. Through extensive experiments on various ViTs and vision tasks, including image classification, object detection, and instance segmentation, we demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms existing methods, achieving superior accuracy while ensuring hardware friendliness.

papers.title: KernelBand: Steering LLM-based Kernel Optimization via Hardware-Aware Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.abstract: High-performance GPU kernels are critical for efficient LLM serving, yet their optimization remains a bottleneck requiring deep system expertise. While code LLMs show promise in generating functionally correct code, kernel optimization is intrinsically a search problem over a vast optimization space. This fundamental mismatch prevents existing LLM agents from efficiently exploring the optimization space for diverse hardware and compute patterns. To bridge the gap, we present KernelBand, a framework that formulates kernel optimization as a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) problem, explicitly balancing exploration and exploitation to unlock the potential of code LLMs. To navigate the infinite arm space of optimization strategies applied to candidate kernels, we design two key mechanisms: a hardware-aware pruning strategy via profiling bounds and a runtime-behavior clustering algorithm that leverages Lipschitz continuity. Extensive experiments on TritonBench-G with three GPU architectures and four code LLMs show that KernelBand consistently outperforms the strongest available agent baseline, achieving up to **1.91×** geometric mean speedup over correctly optimized kernels with **39–140%** relative improvement in Fast@1 success rate. Our code is available at https://github.com/TongmingLAIC/KernelBand.

papers.title: KernelFoundry: Hardware-Aware Evolutionary GPU Kernel Optimization
papers.abstract: GPU kernel optimization challenges LLMs beyond standard coding tasks, as it requires an understanding of hardware architecture, parallel computing optimization strategies, and profiling outputs. However, most existing approaches leveraging LLMs for kernel generation apply standard prompting and feedback loops, considering hardware only through profiling feedback. We introduce KernelFoundry, an evolutionary framework that efficiently explores the space of GPU kernels through (1) MAP-Elites quality-diversity search with kernel-specific behavioral dimensions to sustain exploration; (2) meta-prompt evolution that co-evolves prompts with kernels to uncover task-specific optimization strategies, and (3) a template-based parameter optimization approach to tune kernels to inputs and hardware. We evaluate this framework on KernelBench, robust-kbench and custom tasks, generating SYCL kernels as a cross-platform GPU programming paradigm, and CUDA kernels for comparison to prior work. Our approach consistently outperforms the baseline methods and achieves an average speedup of 2.3 on KernelBench for SYCL. Moreover, KernelFoundry is implemented as a distributed framework with remote access to diverse hardware, allowing quick benchmarking and featuring a flexible user input layer to support kernel generation for a wide range of real use cases beyond benchmarking.

papers.title: Ave: Guiding Agentic GPU Optimization Using Data-Flow Invariants
papers.abstract: LLM coding agents can generate correct GPU kernels, yet their performance still lags behind expert libraries. Achieving peak GPU throughput requires coordinating low-level transformations such as shared-memory staging, software pipelining, and instruction scheduling. Unit tests and performance profiles provide only sparse end-to-end feedback, leaving agents unable to localize violations of the global constraints that these transformations must preserve. We present Ave, an agentic framework that uses data-flow invariants as compile-time guardrails for kernel optimization. These invariants specify relationships among data values that must hold throughout execution. Ave's tile-based Pythonic DSL exposes hardware instructions and compiler policies while abstracting complex memory layout encodings as tiles. Tag functions assign symbolic labels derived from selected logical coordinates and expressions. The compiler propagates these labels through data and control flow, and tag assertions enforce required relationships among them at use sites. The compiler checks these assertions with a tractable, flow-sensitive, path-insensitive analysis backed by an SMT solver, returning concrete assignments that witness abstract violations and guide repairs with no runtime overhead. An in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) planner proposes optimizations from a curated knowledge base. A lowering agent implements them and instantiates their invariants. We evaluate Ave on AMD MI300X across GEMM, flash attention, and MoE, which together account for up to 90% of GPU time in LLM inference. With GPT-5.6 Sol, its optimized kernels achieve 89-99% of the effective throughput of state-of-the-art hand-optimized libraries and improve geometric-mean throughput by 1.62-1176× over uncontaminated agentic baselines. On 200 KernelBench tasks, with GPT-5.6 Sol and in-context DSL examples, Ave produces valid kernels within three attempts for 100% of Level 1 and 88% of Level 2 problems. Ave is open source at https://github.com/causalflowai/avelang.

papers.title: Unleash All Cores: {Asymmetry-Aware} Scalable {DNN} Inference on Mobile {CPUs}
papers.abstract: Asymmetric Multiprocessing (AMP) CPUs are now central to mobile devices, but exploiting them for efficient Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference remains challenging. Naive scheduling across heterogeneous cores often triggers a performance-collapse paradox: adding LITTLE cores degrades throughput due to workload imbalance. Existing approaches rely on static partitioning, which partially mitigates imbalance but fails to adapt to runtime interference, incurs extra task acquisition overhead, and ignores core–kernel affinities—leaving substantial performance untapped. We present SANI, a scalable, asymmetry-aware inference framework that unleashes the full potential of AMP architectures. SANI introduces three key mechanisms: (1) an affinity-aware kernel issuer that selects cluster-optimal kernels to exploit core–kernel efficiency from the outset; (2) an adaptive granularity scheduler that dynamically merges or splits tasks, balancing load under runtime interference by mapping smaller tasks to slower cores and larger ones to faster cores; and (3) an on-demand kernel switcher that efficiently transforms kernels during workload migration, preserving affinity across clusters. We implement SANI atop Arm-CL and evaluate it on five mobile SoCs. SANI reduces DNN inference latency by 17.6%–23.7% on average (up to 29.5% on some models) while lowering energy consumption by up to 39% compared to state-of-the-art baselines, scaling efficiently across both symmetric and asymmetric CPU configurations.

papers.title: UniSVQ: 2-bit Unified Scalar-Vector Quantization
papers.abstract:
Post-training quantization at the 2-bit level enables low-cost deployment and inference acceleration for large language models (LLMs). Scalar quantization (SQ) and vector quantization (VQ) are two primary quantization methods, however, the former suffers from significant performance degradation, and the latter incurs computational and storage overhead. 
We propose UniSVQ, a unified 2-bit quantization framework that bridges scalar and vector quantization by parameterizing codewords as an affine transform of integer lattices.
This structure preserves compatibility with optimized integer kernels while retaining much of VQ's flexibility. 
We further introduce a data-driven block-wise fine-tuning strategy to directly minimize quantization reconstruction error.
Extensive experiments across multiple LLM families and zero-shot benchmarks demonstrate that UniSVQ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art SQ methods and achieves performance comparable to advanced VQ methods, while providing higher inference throughput.

papers.title: EGG: An Expert-Guided Agent Framework for Kernel Generation
papers.abstract: High-performance GPU kernels are critical for reducing the exponentially growing computational costs of large language models (LLMs), but their development heavily relies on manual tuning by domain experts. While recent advances in LLM-based approaches show promise for automating kernel generation, they still struggle to achieve both correctness and high performance. This limitation primarily arises from the lack of domain-specific optimization guidance, hindering effective exploration of the optimization space. We propose $\textbf{EGG}$, an $\underline{E}$xpert-$\underline{G}$uided Agent Framework for Kernel $\underline{G}$eneration, which incorporates expert optimization principles to guide LLMs’ decisions. Inspired by expert workflows, we decompose kernel generation into two hierarchical stages: 1) algorithmic structure design, which establishes a high-quality computational structure foundation; 2) hardware-specific tuning, which performs targeted adjustments through parallel mapping, tensor tiling, and memory optimization. This staged decomposition defines explicit optimization objectives, structuring the design space to achieve progressive refinements. To this end, a stage-aware multi-agent collaboration mechanism is designed for inter and intra-stage context management, ensuring stable optimization trajectories. Experiments on KernelBench and real-world workloads show that EGG achieves a $2.13\times$ average speedup over PyTorch, outperforming existing agent-based and RL-based approaches.

papers.title: FourTune: Towards Fully 4-Bit Efficient Post-Training for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract:
Diffusion models have become a dominant paradigm for high-quality generative modeling, while post-training is essential for adapting them to diverse downstream applications.
However, post-training of large diffusion models is still challenging due to the prohibitive memory footprints and slow training speed, which existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods only partially address.
To overcome these limitations, we propose FourTune, an efficient post-training framework for diffusion models based on an end-to-end W4A4G4 paradigm. FourTune introduces a triple-branch hybrid pipeline that augments the standard LoRA architecture with a frozen numerical stabilizer to isolate quantization-sensitive outliers, enabling stable training under native 4-bit computation. In addition, FourTune employs hardware-efficient block-wise quantization and customized fused kernels to support efficient quantized backpropagation and reduce memory bandwidth overhead.
Across customization, reinforcement learning, and distillation tasks, FourTune matches the quality of full-precision fine-tuning. On FLUX.1-dev (12B), FourTune reduces memory overhead by $2.25\times$ and increases end-to-end training throughput by $2.27\times$ compared to BF16 LoRA.

papers.title: Exploring Layer-wise Information Effectiveness for Post-Training Quantization in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models with billions of parameters are often over-provisioned: many layers contribute little unique information yet dominate the memory and energy footprint during inference. We present LieQ (Layer-wise information effectiveness Quantization), a hardware-native, metric-driven post-training quantization framework that addresses the critical challenge of maintaining accuracy in sub-8B models, model parameters less than 8B, under extreme low-bit compression. LieQ keeps uniform bit-width within each layer while mixing precision across layers, preserving standard multiplication kernels and avoiding irregular memory access, codebooks, or irregular formats at inference time. Our method uncovers a strong correlation between layer-wise functional saliency and representational compactness, revealing that layers with higher training-induced energy concentration are functionally irreplaceable. Leveraging this insight, we propose a purely geometry-driven sensitivity proxy that enables automatic bit-width allocation under a target average-bit budget without expensive gradient updates or inference-based perplexity probing. Under an average weight bit-width approaching two bits per parameter, LieQ consistently reduces the large accuracy gap typically observed for naive uniform 2-bit baselines on Qwen3 and LLaMA3.x families, while retaining standard-kernel efficiency. These properties make LieQ a practical path toward deploying small language models on resource-constrained edge devices. Code will be available at: https://github.com/HeXiao-55/LieQ-official.git.

papers.title: Sparser, Faster, Lighter Transformer Language Models
papers.abstract: Scaling autoregressive large language models (LLMs) has driven unprecedented progress but comes with vast computational costs. In this work, we tackle these costs by leveraging unstructured sparsity within an LLM's feedforward layers, the components accounting for most of the model parameters and execution FLOPs. To achieve this, we introduce a new sparse packing format and a set of CUDA kernels designed to seamlessly integrate with the optimized execution pipelines of modern GPUs, enabling efficient sparse computation during LLM inference and training. To substantiate our gains, we provide a quantitative study of LLM sparsity, demonstrating that simple L1 regularization can induce over 99% sparsity with negligible impact on downstream performance. When paired with our kernels, we show that these sparsity levels translate into substantial throughput, energy efficiency, and memory usage benefits that increase with model scale. We will release all code and kernels under an open-source license to promote adoption and accelerate research toward establishing sparsity as a practical axis for improving the efficiency and scalability of modern foundation models.

llm_ranked.tldr_en: SANI is an asymmetry-aware inference framework that schedules DNN kernels across heterogeneous mobile CPU cores with affinity awareness, avoiding the throughput collapse caused by naive LITTLE-core scheduling.

llm_ranked.title_zh: 释放所有核心：移动CPU上非对称感知的可扩展DNN推理

llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出SANI框架，采用核亲和感知的算子调度、动态负载均衡与运行时干扰自适应三项机制。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实验显示SANI避免小核加入带来的性能崩塌，充分利用异构核心并显著提升DNN推理吞吐。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 该工作表明亲和感知调度可释放移动CPU多核潜力，为端侧推理加速提供通用调度范式。

llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 跨GPU、NPU、FPGA硬件后端并结合算子变换的延迟预测
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Accurate latency prediction is needed to pick optimal model strategies across heterogeneous hardware. CloserToMe models NN-structure and device execution interactions instead of black-box regression, enabling transferable prediction across GPU, NPU and FPGA backends.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 面向异构设备选择最优模型优化策略需要准确的延迟预测，但现有方法把硬件当作黑盒直接回归，忽略了网络结构与设备执行行为的交互。本文提出统一的建模框架，显式刻画算子变换与结构修改在不同硬件后端上的执行特性。实验表明该框架能在GPU、NPU与FPGA之间实现更准确且可迁移的延迟预测，从而加速后端策略选择。
llm_ranked.title_zh: CloserToMe：面向异构设备的准确可迁移延迟预测统一框架
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 异构设备上选择模型优化策略需要准确延迟预测，现有黑盒回归方法忽略结构与硬件的执行交互。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出统一建模框架，显式刻画神经网络结构与GPU、NPU、FPGA等设备执行行为之间的交互关系。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实验表明该框架在多种硬件后端上取得更准确且可跨设备迁移的延迟预测效果。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 显式建模结构-硬件交互可提升延迟预测的准确性与可迁移性，助力跨后端策略快速选择。

llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 通过张量变换将自定义低精度类型映射到硬件的编译器
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Low-precision computing is hampered by poor hardware support for evolving custom data types. Ladder is a compiler with a tType type system and extended tensor expressions that transforms low-precision tensors into hardware-supported formats for real speedups.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 低精度计算有望提升深度学习性能，但现有软硬件对不断涌现的自定义数据类型支持不足，难以获得真实加速。本文提出Ladder编译器，借助通用类型系统tType与扩展的张量表达式，将低精度张量变换为硬件支持的格式。该工作弥合了自定义数据类型与固定硬件精度之间的鸿沟，为低精度算子执行提供通用编译支持。
llm_ranked.title_zh: Ladder：通过硬件感知张量变换实现高效低精度深度学习计算
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 低精度计算有潜力，但现有软硬件对新兴自定义数据类型支持不足，难以获得真实性能提升。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出Ladder编译器，基于通用类型系统tType和扩展张量表达式做硬件感知的张量变换。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 将低精度张量映射为硬件支持的精度格式，从而在现有硬件上实现低精度计算加速。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 通过编译期张量变换可弥合自定义低精度类型与固定硬件格式之间的差距。

llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 将张量程序巨型内核化并实现跨算子流水线
llm_ranked.tldr_en: MPK compiles multi-GPU tensor inference into a single persistent mega-kernel, using an SM-level graph to enable cross-operator pipelining and computation-communication overlap beyond the kernel-per-operator model.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对传统逐算子执行模型难以实现跨算子流水线和通信计算重叠的问题，MPK提出首个自动将多GPU模型推理转换为单一高性能巨型内核的编译器和运行时。它构建SM级任务图，将张量程序编译为优化任务并生成CUDA实现，由持久化巨型内核运行时执行。该设计使跨算子软件流水线和细粒度通信计算重叠成为可能，从而提升多GPU推理性能。
llm_ranked.title_zh: MPK：面向张量程序巨型内核化的编译器和运行时
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 传统逐算子执行模型难以实现跨算子流水线和通信计算重叠，限制多GPU推理性能。
llm_ranked.method_cn: MPK构建SM级任务图，将张量程序编译为优化任务并生成CUDA实现，由持久化巨型内核运行时执行。
llm_ranked.result_cn: MPK能把多GPU模型推理自动转换为单一高性能巨型内核，并支持细粒度流水与重叠。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 该工作为张量程序提供了超越逐算子执行的新型编译与运行时范式。

llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 以数据流不变量作为GPU内核优化的编译期护栏
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Ave uses data-flow invariants as compile-time guardrails to guide LLM coding agents in optimizing GPU kernels, coordinating shared-memory staging, pipelining and instruction scheduling for higher throughput.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对LLM编码智能体生成的GPU内核虽正确但性能落后于专家库、且单元测试和性能剖析反馈稀疏的问题，Ave提出以数据流不变量作为编译期护栏的智能体优化框架。它通过基于Tile的Python DSL暴露硬件指令和编译策略，帮助智能体定位并保持全局约束。该工作为GPU内核自动优化提供了可迁移方法，可启发算子内核性能调优。
llm_ranked.title_zh: Ave：利用数据流不变量指导智能体GPU优化
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: LLM智能体生成的GPU内核虽正确，但性能仍落后于专家库，且现有反馈稀疏。
llm_ranked.method_cn: Ave以数据流不变量作为编译期护栏，结合Tile级Python DSL指导智能体进行GPU内核优化。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 该框架帮助智能体协调共享内存、流水线和指令调度等底层变换，从而提升GPU吞吐。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: Ave为算子内核的智能体化性能优化提供了可迁移的编译期约束方法。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: hardware-aware quantization aligned to MAC circuit behavior
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 对齐MAC电路特性的硬件感知量化
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 对齐MAC电路特性的硬件感知量化
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Conventional quantization ignores circuit-level timing and energy of MAC units. HALO is a hardware-aware post-training quantization framework incorporating critical-path delay, better exploiting timing margins and energy savings on accelerators.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 该文针对传统量化与硬件无关、忽略乘加单元时序与能耗特性的问题，提出硬件感知的训练后量化框架HALO。它显式引入关键路径延迟等电路级硬件特征来指导权重量化，从而利用可用时序余量与节能空间。研究旨在提升现代加速器上的部署效率，为量化算子与硬件协同的高效执行提供方法支撑。
llm_ranked.title_zh: HALO：面向LLM加速的低关键路径延迟权重硬件感知量化
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 传统量化与硬件无关，忽略MAC单元时序与能耗，难以发挥加速器效率。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出硬件感知训练后量化框架，引入关键路径延迟等电路特征指导量化。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 借助硬件时序与能耗特征利用时序余量，提升加速器上的部署效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 该方法把电路级硬件特性纳入量化，为量化算子高效硬件执行提供支撑。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Benchmark for agentic low-level kernel generation on emerging accelerators
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向新兴加速器的智能体底层内核生成基准
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向新兴加速器的智能体底层内核生成基准
llm_ranked.tldr_en: KernelCraft is the first benchmark evaluating whether agentic LLM systems can generate and optimize valid, efficient low-level kernels for emerging accelerators with novel ISAs through a function-calling, feedback-driven workflow.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对新兴AI加速器ISA需要手工编写底层内核、耗时且难以跨硬件扩展的问题，本文提出KernelCraft基准。它通过函数调用与反馈驱动的流程，评估LLM智能体为定制加速器生成并优化底层内核的能力。实验在多类新兴硬件上刻画了智能体生成有效高效内核的表现。其贡献在于为算子内核的自动化生成与硬件适配提供了首个系统性评测平台。
llm_ranked.title_zh: KernelCraft：面向新兴硬件的智能体近金属内核生成基准
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 新兴加速器需手工编写底层内核，耗时易错且难以跨硬件目标扩展。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建KernelCraft基准，以函数调用与反馈驱动流程评测智能体生成底层内核的能力。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多类新兴ISA硬件上刻画了智能体生成有效且高效内核的表现。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为算子内核自动化生成与硬件适配提供了首个系统性评测平台。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: high-performance prefix-sum kernels on Ascend NPU accelerator
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向昇腾NPU加速器的高性能前缀和算子内核
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向昇腾NPU加速器的高性能前缀和算子内核
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This work designs high-performance prefix-sum (scan) kernels for the Ascend NPU, exploiting vector and matrix units to reach up to 74.9% of memory-copy bandwidth and accelerating common AI/LLM computational primitives.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 大模型部署需针对硬件优化少量通用并行原语，而前缀和（scan）在昇腾NPU上缺乏高效实现。本文设计面向昇腾架构的高性能scan算法，充分利用向量与矩阵单元，最高达到内存拷贝带宽的74.9%。作者将其作为快速原语应用于多个AI与LLM工作负载，验证了实际加速效果。该工作展示了算子内核针对特定硬件加速器优化的一般方法。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 昇腾AI加速器上的并行扫描
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 大模型需要针对特定硬件优化通用并行原语，而前缀和在昇腾NPU上缺乏高效算子实现。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 设计面向昇腾架构的高性能scan算法，充分利用向量与矩阵单元提升带宽利用率。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 达到内存拷贝带宽的74.9%，并在多个AI与LLM工作负载中实现加速。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 表明针对硬件加速器定制算子内核可有效加速通用计算原语。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: hardware-aware kernel optimization search for accelerated inference
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向加速推理的硬件感知内核优化搜索
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向加速推理的硬件感知内核优化搜索
llm_ranked.tldr_en: KernelBand formulates GPU kernel optimization as a multi-armed bandit problem, balancing exploration and exploitation to steer code LLMs through the vast optimization space for diverse hardware and compute patterns.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 高性能GPU内核优化依赖深厚系统经验，而代码大模型虽能生成正确代码却难以高效搜索庞大优化空间。KernelBand将内核优化建模为多臂老虎机问题，显式平衡探索与利用以引导代码大模型。该框架针对不同硬件与计算模式搜索优化策略，提升了内核优化的效率。其硬件感知搜索思路可迁移至算子内核的性能优化。
llm_ranked.title_zh: KernelBand：以硬件感知多臂老虎机引导基于LLM的内核优化
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: GPU内核优化依赖专家经验，现有代码大模型难以高效探索庞大的优化空间。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出KernelBand，将内核优化建模为多臂老虎机问题，平衡探索与利用引导LLM搜索。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多样硬件与计算模式下更高效地搜索内核优化策略。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为算子内核的自动化性能优化提供了硬件感知的可迁移搜索框架。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: deeply fused kernel cutting memory traffic for accelerated inference
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 通过深度算子融合降低访存以加速推理
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 通过深度算子融合降低访存以加速推理
llm_ranked.tldr_en: DeepFusionKernel deeply fuses SwiGLU MLP blocks to cut HBM traffic and boost cache reuse, delivering up to 13.2% speedup on H100 and 9.7% on A100 over SGLang with a companion kernel scheduler.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 长上下文智能体推理受限于内存带宽而非算力，SwiGLU MLP块因权重超出缓存成为未被充分优化的瓶颈。本文提出DeepFusionKernel，通过深度算子融合减少HBM访存并提升缓存复用。在H100上相较SGLang最高提速13.2%，A100上提速9.7%，并配合内核调度器保持稳定加速。该工作体现了算子融合与内存布局优化对推理加速的价值。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 面向Transformer的深度算子融合
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 长上下文推理受内存带宽限制，SwiGLU MLP块因权重超缓存成为未优化瓶颈。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出DeepFusionKernel，通过深度算子融合降低HBM访存并提升缓存复用，配合内核调度器。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在H100上相较SGLang最高提速13.2%，A100上提速9.7%。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 表明算子融合与内存优化可显著提升推理加速效果且适配多平台。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: GPU-optimized SpMV kernel co-design for accelerated sparse inference
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向稀疏推理加速的GPU优化SpMV内核协同设计
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向稀疏推理加速的GPU优化SpMV内核协同设计
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Sparse LLM inference relies on SpMV, but existing methods perform poorly under low unstructured sparsity. MACKO co-designs a GPU-friendly storage format and kernel, identifying memory bandwidth as the bottleneck and achieving speedups at 50 percent sparsity.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 稀疏大模型推理依赖稀疏矩阵向量乘，但现有方法在30-90%的低非结构化稀疏度下性能不佳，内存收益和加速有限。本文提出MACKO，将存储格式与GPU内核协同设计，使其契合GPU执行模型并降低存储开销。作者指出内存带宽是主要瓶颈，实验显示在50%稀疏度下首次取得显著加速，为稀疏推理提供高效内核方案。
llm_ranked.title_zh: MACKO：面向低稀疏度的稀疏矩阵向量乘
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 剪枝大模型的低非结构化稀疏度下，现有SpMV方法内存收益与加速有限。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出GPU优化的存储格式与内核协同设计的MACKO-SpMV，并分析存储开销与带宽瓶颈。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在50%稀疏度下首次实现显著加速，无需专用硬件单元或预计算。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 格式与内核协同设计可在低稀疏度下有效提升SpMV性能，支撑稀疏大模型推理。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Fused Triton kernels with tiling and on-chip memory streaming for operator fusion
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 采用分块与片上内存流式的融合Triton内核实现算子融合
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 采用分块与片上内存流式的融合Triton内核实现算子融合
llm_ranked.tldr_en: GPU Sinkhorn solvers suffer quadratic HBM traffic and limited kernel fusion. FlashSinkhorn rewrites log-domain updates as row-wise LogSumExp reductions, enabling FlashAttention-style fused Triton kernels that stream tiles through SRAM for IO efficiency.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 基于Sinkhorn迭代的熵正则最优传输在GPU上规模扩展时效率低下，稠密实现带来二次HBM流量，在线后端又缺乏内核融合。本文提出FlashSinkhorn，将对数域更新改写为带偏置点积的行级LogSumExp归约，从而支持FlashAttention式的分块与融合。融合Triton内核将数据块流经片上SRAM，显著降低IO开销并提升大规模求解效率。
llm_ranked.title_zh: FlashSinkhorn：GPU上IO感知的熵正则最优传输
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: GPU上Sinkhorn求解器规模扩展时存在二次HBM流量与内核融合不足的效率问题。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 将对数域更新改写为行级LogSumExp归约，采用FlashAttention式分块与融合Triton内核。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 融合内核通过片上SRAM流式处理数据块，降低IO开销并提升大规模求解效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: IO感知的算子融合与分块策略可显著提升GPU上熵正则最优传输的可扩展性。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Automated high-performance GPU kernel generation via expert-guided LLM agents
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 通过专家引导的LLM智能体自动生成高性能GPU内核
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 通过专家引导的LLM智能体自动生成高性能GPU内核
llm_ranked.tldr_en: EGG is an expert-guided agent framework that injects domain optimization principles into LLM decisions to automatically generate correct and high-performance GPU kernels, decomposing kernel generation into expert-like workflows.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对LLM计算开销激增而高性能GPU内核依赖专家手工调优、LLM自动生成难以兼顾正确性与性能的问题，本文提出EGG专家引导智能体框架，将专家优化原则注入LLM的决策过程。方法上仿照专家工作流把内核生成分解为可引导的阶段，约束优化空间探索。实验表明该框架能生成更正确且高效的内核。其意义在于为算子内核自动优化提供了可迁移的智能体范式。
llm_ranked.title_zh: EGG：面向内核生成的专家引导智能体框架
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 高性能GPU内核开发依赖专家手工调优，现有LLM方法难以同时保证正确性与高性能。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出专家引导的智能体框架，将专家优化原则注入LLM决策并分解内核生成流程。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实验显示该框架生成的内核在正确性与性能上均优于缺乏领域引导的基线。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为算子内核的自动化生成与优化提供了可复用的智能体范式。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: operator kernel optimization for accelerated inference

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Using matrix multiplication units to execute segmented deep learning operations on accelerators
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 利用矩阵乘法单元在加速器上执行分段深度学习运算
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 利用矩阵乘法单元在加速器上执行分段深度学习运算
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper proposes MMV-RAM, a computational model extending Vector-RAM with a matrix multiplication unit, enabling fundamental deep learning operations to be executed as segmented matrix multiplications on otherwise underutilized AI accelerator MMUs.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对现代AI加速器中矩阵乘法单元除稠密矩阵乘外常被闲置、缺乏理论计算模型的问题，本文提出MMV-RAM模型，在向量RAM基础上加入矩阵乘法单元。方法通过分段运算将基本深度学习操作映射为小矩阵乘，并给出计算能力平衡的理论分析。分析表明该模型可高效执行更多算子。其意义在于为加速器上的算子执行与算法设计提供理论指导。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 使用矩阵乘法的分段运算
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: AI加速器的矩阵乘法单元在稠密矩阵乘之外常被闲置，且缺乏严谨计算模型。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出MMV-RAM模型，在向量RAM上增加矩阵乘法单元并以分段矩阵乘执行基本运算。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 给出矩阵与向量单元计算能力平衡的理论分析及分段运算的可行性证明。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为加速器上张量算子的高效执行与算法设计提供了理论模型基础。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: hardware acceleration for tensor operator execution

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Hardware-native post-training quantization preserving standard multiplication kernels
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 保持标准乘法内核的硬件友好训练后量化
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 保持标准乘法内核的硬件友好训练后量化
llm_ranked.tldr_en: LieQ is a hardware-native, metric-driven post-training quantization framework for sub-8B models that mixes precision across layers while keeping uniform bit-width within each layer, preserving standard multiplication kernels and avoiding irregular memory access at inference.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 针对小型语言模型在极低比特压缩下难以保持精度的挑战，本文提出LieQ逐层信息有效性量化框架。方法依据信息有效性指标在层间混合精度、层内保持统一比特宽度，从而保留标准乘法内核并避免不规则内存访问。实验表明其在亚8B模型极端压缩下仍能维持精度。其贡献在于提供了一种硬件友好的量化方案，兼顾压缩率与部署效率。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 探索小型语言模型训练后量化的逐层信息有效性
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 小型语言模型部分层信息冗余却占用大量内存与能耗，极低比特量化易损失精度。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出LieQ框架，按层信息有效性在层间混合精度并保持层内统一比特宽度。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在亚8B模型极端低比特压缩下保持精度且不引入不规则内存访问。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为硬件友好的高效量化部署提供了兼顾精度与效率的方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: quantized operator kernels for efficient hardware execution

llm_ranked.evidence_en: hardware-friendly uniform quantization enabling accelerator inference
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向加速器推理的硬件友好均匀量化
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向加速器推理的硬件友好均匀量化
llm_ranked.tldr_en: UQ-ViT addresses extreme activation non-uniformity that breaks uniform quantization in Vision Transformers, proposing hardware-friendly quantization that preserves accuracy while keeping accelerator matrix-core inference efficient.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 视觉Transformer中后Softmax注意力分数呈幂律分布、后GELU激活通道间方差大，导致均匀量化难以兼顾高幅值精度与整体误差。UQ-ViT提出硬件友好的均匀量化方案，通过激活整形与校准缓解极端非均匀性。实验表明其在保持精度的同时可充分利用加速器矩阵核心实现高效推理。该工作为量化算子内核在硬件上的高效执行提供了可迁移思路。
llm_ranked.title_zh: UQ-ViT：以硬件友好均匀量化协调视觉Transformer中的极端激活
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 视觉Transformer激活分布极端非均匀，使均匀量化在保精度与适配加速器之间陷入两难。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出UQ-ViT，用校准与激活整形将极端激活映射到硬件友好的均匀量化范围。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在视觉Transformer量化基准上兼顾精度，同时支持加速器矩阵核心高效推理。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为量化算子内核在硬件加速器上的高效部署提供了硬件友好的量化方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: quantized operator kernels for efficient hardware execution

llm_ranked.evidence_en: implements each quantized operator as a look-up table to simplify quantized operator evaluation
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 用量化算子序列建模推理并以查找表实现每个算子
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 用量化算子序列建模推理并以查找表实现每个算子
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Proposes a PPML paradigm for quantized models that implements each quantized operator as a look-up table, simplifying operator evaluation and cutting protocol overhead.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 量化模型能提升效率，但在隐私保护机器学习中量化算子内部结构复杂，导致现有协议效率低下。本文提出一种面向量化模型的新PPML范式，将推理过程视为量化算子序列，并用查找表实现每个算子以简化求值。该做法可忽略任意函数的复杂内部构造，从而降低量化算子评估的协议开销，为隐私场景下高效利用量化模型提供了新思路。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 面向量化模型的新型PPML范式
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 量化模型在隐私保护机器学习中因量化算子内部结构复杂而导致协议效率低下。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 将推理建模为量化算子序列，并用查找表实现每个算子以简化求值。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 查找表可绕过函数内部复杂构造，降低量化算子评估的协议开销。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为隐私保护场景下高效利用量化模型提供了新范式。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: Quantized operator kernel behavior and constraints in LiteRT

llm_ranked.evidence_en: hardware-aware evolutionary optimization of GPU kernels
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向硬件的GPU算子核进化式优化
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向硬件的GPU算子核进化式优化
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Introduces KernelFoundry, an evolutionary framework using MAP-Elites quality-diversity search, meta-prompt evolution and template tuning to optimize GPU kernels in a hardware-aware way.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: GPU核优化要求理解硬件架构与并行策略，而现有基于大模型的方法仅靠性能剖析反馈考虑硬件，探索能力有限。本文提出KernelFoundry进化框架，通过MAP-Elites质量多样性搜索保持探索，用元提示进化协同挖掘任务相关优化策略，并以模板化参数调优精化核实现。该框架能高效探索GPU核空间，生成更优的硬件感知核，为算子核自动优化提供了可迁移方法。
llm_ranked.title_zh: KernelFoundry：硬件感知的进化式GPU核优化
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有基于大模型的GPU核生成仅通过性能剖析反馈考虑硬件，优化能力有限。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出进化框架，结合MAP-Elites质量多样性搜索、元提示进化与模板化参数调优。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 该框架高效探索GPU核空间，生成更优的硬件感知核实现。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为面向硬件的算子核自动优化提供了可迁移的进化式方法。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: operator kernel optimization for accelerated inference

llm_ranked.evidence_en: 2-bit quantization preserving compatibility with optimized integer kernels
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 2比特量化保持与优化整型核的兼容
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 2比特量化保持与优化整型核的兼容
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Proposes UniSVQ, a unified 2-bit scalar-vector quantization framework that parameterizes codewords as affine integer-lattice transforms, keeping compatibility with optimized integer kernels.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 2比特训练后量化利于大模型低成本部署，但标量量化精度下降明显，矢量量化又带来计算与存储开销。本文提出UniSVQ统一框架，将码字参数化为整数格点的仿射变换，从而在保持与优化整型核兼容的同时保留矢量量化的灵活性，并引入分块微调以最小化重构误差。实验表明该方法在高效硬件执行与精度之间取得良好平衡，为低比特推理提供硬件友好的量化方案。
llm_ranked.title_zh: UniSVQ：2比特统一标量-矢量量化
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 2比特量化利于大模型低成本部署，但标量量化精度差、矢量量化开销大。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出统一框架，将码字参数化为整数格点仿射变换，兼顾整型核兼容与矢量灵活性，并做分块微调。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实验表明该方法在保持整型核兼容的同时取得优于标量量化的精度。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为2比特高效推理提供了兼顾精度与硬件友好的量化方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: quantized operator kernels for efficient hardware execution

llm_ranked.evidence_en: CUDA kernels for efficient sparse inference on GPUs
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向GPU高效稀疏推理的CUDA内核
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向GPU高效稀疏推理的CUDA内核
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This work introduces a sparse packing format and custom CUDA kernels integrated into GPU execution pipelines, enabling efficient sparse LLM inference and training with over 99 percent sparsity.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 大型语言模型计算成本高昂，本文利用前馈层非结构化稀疏降低开销。方法提出新的稀疏打包格式与配套CUDA内核，无缝接入现代GPU优化执行管线，从而高效支持稀疏推理与训练。定量研究表明简单L1正则即可带来超过99%稀疏度且对下游性能影响甚微。该工作为算子级内核优化与硬件加速推理提供了可复用方法。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 更稀疏、更快、更轻的Transformer语言模型
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: LLM计算成本高，前馈层参数与FLOPs占比大。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出稀疏打包格式与CUDA内核并接入GPU执行管线。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现超99%稀疏度且下游性能几乎无损。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为稀疏推理提供内核级硬件加速方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: operator kernel optimization for accelerated inference

llm_ranked.evidence_en: End-to-end W4A4G4 4-bit quantization pipeline for efficient execution
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向高效执行的端到端W4A4G4四位量化流程
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向高效执行的端到端W4A4G4四位量化流程
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Post-training large diffusion models is limited by memory and speed. FourTune introduces an end-to-end W4A4G4 framework with a triple-branch hybrid pipeline and frozen numerical stabilizer to isolate quantization-sensitive outliers for stable 4-bit training.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 扩散模型的后训练受限于巨大内存开销与缓慢训练速度，现有参数高效微调方法只能部分缓解。本文提出FourTune，一种端到端W4A4G4的四位后训练框架，通过三分支混合流水线结合冻结的数值稳定器来隔离量化敏感离群值。该设计使模型能在原生四位精度下稳定训练，为低精度高效后训练提供可行路径。
llm_ranked.title_zh: FourTune：面向扩散模型的全四位高效后训练
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 扩散模型后训练内存开销大、速度慢，现有参数高效微调方法难以充分缓解。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出端到端W4A4G4框架，采用三分支混合流水线加冻结数值稳定器隔离量化敏感离群值。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 使扩散模型可在原生四位精度下稳定训练，降低内存并提升后训练效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 端到端低精度后训练框架可在保持稳定的同时显著降低扩散模型后训练成本。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: quantized operator kernels for efficient hardware execution
